thread:
SupportAlex: Heads-up — Acme reported streaming API (SSE) sessions dropping ~30s in and clients reconnecting but missing the final tokens. They're seeing partial outputs and duplicate messages on reconnects. Ticket #ACME-894 attached.
Matt_SRE: Can you paste the client's curl/devstack repro and any server-side request IDs? Also did they say this started after a deploy? :thinking:
SupportAlex: Repro steps from the customer below. No deploy from our side at that time. They claim it started after they switched to our dedicated endpoint. Steps:
```
# reproduce
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDDO_API_KEY" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=llama-3-8b&stream=true" 
# client observes disconnect after ~30s. On reconnect they see the stream resumed but last chunk missing.
```
Acme_Eng: adding logs — we see a final "event: output" that never arrives. TCP FIN followed by client reconnect within 300ms. No 5xx from API.
Luis_Eng: Ok — two likely layers: ALB/ELB or a proxy killing idle connections; or our server hitting a per-request write timeout. Can you upload a pcap and slow-wire dump? Also need the request-id header (x-request-id) from the customer's initial request.
Acme_Eng: uploaded pcap and a HAR to our S3. Link: https://files.acme.com/repro/1770034567_streaming_pcaps.tar.gz (they also handed over our header x-request-id: 0a7c9f2d)
ingest-bot: pcap uploaded to internal bucket: https://files.redwood.com/pcap/1770034567.pcap
SupportAlex: I attached the customer's server logs too. Not seeing application errors, just a stream write that stops. snippet:
```
2026-03-11T14:02:18.123Z INFO stream write start req=0a7c9f2d
2026-03-11T14:02:47.341Z WARN stream write partial bytes=452 req=0a7c9f2d
2026-03-11T14:02:47.342Z INFO connection closed remote=10.12.3.45:39872 req=0a7c9f2d
```
Matt_SRE: That aligns with a mid-stream connection termination. Two follow-ups: 1) check ALB idle-timeout and NGINX proxy send timeout; 2) capture server-side send buffer stats and any TLS alerts. Can someone grep for RST or FIN in the pcap?
Luis_Eng: I pulled the pcap — seeing a TCP RST from the client IP after a burst of data. Also an HTTP/2 GOAWAY from ALB shortly before. Summary:
- 14:02:47.340: ALB sends HTTP/2 GOAWAY (max-stream-id 789)
- 14:02:47.341: TCP RST from client
This suggests the ALB is rebalancing or hitting a circuit breaker.
Carla_Product: Do we have any metrics showing per-route drop or stream errors around that time? I want to correlate with releases and scaling events.
deploy-bot: autoscaler:scaled_down service=streaming-runtime zone=us-east-1a reason=cpu_idle threshold=20% time=2026-03-11T14:02:40Z
Matt_SRE: Aha — autoscaler scaled down a pod at 14:02:40Z, which could have triggered ALB drain behavior causing the GOAWAY. That lines up with the timing.
Luis_Eng: Root cause hypothesis: pod scaled down (or node drained) -> ALB issues GOAWAY to gracefully close streams -> client receives GOAWAY then issues reconnect but misses final event if we didn't replay/ack. The fact they see duplicate messages on reconnect implies our resume token handling isn't idempotent.
Acme_Eng: We also see this pattern occasionally under load; they lose ~2-3% of streaming responses when bursts + scale events coincide.
SupportAlex: Customer wants a mitigation ASAP — either ensure graceful drain preserves SSE final events or make client reconnect behavior deterministic (resume token or idempotent markers). Suggestions?
Matt_SRE: Short-term: increase ALB connection draining window and bump autoscaler cooldown for streaming pool. Also add an exp-backoff in client to fetch missing end-state via non-streaming endpoint after reconnect. Mid-term: implement server-side ephemeral resume tokens so reconnections request missing suffix.
Luis_Eng: I'm going to open an infra change PR: increase ALB idle_timeout to 120s for streaming listeners and add "drain-delay" to the autoscaler when active_streams > 0. Will add an observability metric: stream_graceful_close_count and stream_unexpected_termination_count.
Carla_Product: Also notify account team and offer Acme a temporary dedicated pool throttle or reserved instance to avoid scale churn.
SupportAlex: I'll send the customer a note: root-cause hypothesis + immediate mitigations (ALB timeout bump, autoscaler cooldown, client workaround). Will ask them to run a new repro after we change infra.
Matt_SRE: Before infra change, can we reproduce internally with a synthetic client that opens many long-lived SSE connections and then triggers scale-down? I'll spin it up and attach logs.
Luis_Eng: Test plan:
1) start 200 SSE clients with long-poll
2) generate traffic to keep model tokens streaming for 60s
3) trigger scale-down by lowering target cpu or issuing scale command
4) capture pcap and server traces
I'll run tonight and post results.
SupportAlex: Thanks — I've escalated to infra and left a provisional support ticket note. Acme asked for an ETA; tell them we'll have a mitigation plan within 48h. :thumbsup:
Matt_SRE: Also add a quick server-side change: if pod sees active stream count > 0, avoid immediate close on SIGTERM; sleep 20s to allow streams to finish if possible.
Acme_Eng: Appreciate it. We'll re-run once you confirm the changes. If you need our logs again, ping.
ingest-bot: traces uploaded: https://traces.redwood.com/trace/0a7c9f2d
SupportAlex: Closing loop: tagging this thread for eng-oncall and infra change. Will update ticket when PRs are merged.
__notes: This thread simulates an escalated support issue about SSE streaming disconnects, includes pcap/upload links, logs, autoscaler events, and suggested mitigations. All fields are flat strings or list of strings per agents.md.
